Two in-place fixes surfaced by the suite: (a) E2E-3.1 deviates from the plan's prescribed 5 ms logger BY DESIGN — the ready→first-paint gap is one setTimeout(0) + ~1 ms extraction ≈ 1.5–4 ms, sub-poll-period, so a 5 ms poll cannot order the two one-shot transitions (P(miss the gap) ≈ gap/period ≈ 30–80 % flake); in-page MutationObservers record each transition at its exact performance.now() timestamp instead — new learning doc written; (b) the B-04 (rev) template pin in BeatDotsTest.html pinned the pre-CR .progress[role=progressbar] markup and failed on the W-10 role move — updated in place to assert the role on .progress-readout with :aria-valuetext=formattedDisplayPosition and NOT on .progress (the settled W-10 disposition supersedes the v1 pin; the N-10 static-label rule travels with it). Success-criteria grep pass: progress-fill zero in index.html/Style.css (a self-referencing comment in the CSS had to be reworded — the grep is literal); progressPercent zero template consumers (computed retained per R-4); zero requestAnimationFrame in createMetronomadMethods.js (D9). key_decisions: setPeaks is called from _runPeakExtraction's guarded write (if (this._waveformView) this._waveformView.setPeaks(this._peaks)) — resolves the Phase-3 handoff question ('can Phase 4 call setPeaks from the VM?') in the most direct way: same guarded site that writes _peaks/waveformReady, no watcher, no extra reactive flip; the mock-VM rows leave _waveformView undefined and the guard makes them view-agnostic

_schedulePostLoadTasks stays inside onFileDropped's try block (D-E verbatim position): it cannot realistically throw (both tasks are async no-throw-to-first-await; extractPeaks is guarded), so the catch's spurious-errorMessage risk is theoretical — followed the pinned shape

E2E-3.1 uses MutationObservers instead of the plan's prescribed 5 ms logger: the ordering assertion needs a sample strictly inside the ready→paint gap, and that gap (1.5–4 ms) is shorter than the 5 ms period — a coin-flip flake by construction. The deviation is documented in the spec header and the learning doc; the 5 ms logger remains the convention for continuous signals (E2E-3.2 uses it unchanged, same file)

Unit rows drive the pinned setTimeout(0) yield by swapping window.setTimeout for a FIFO (withPinnedYields helper, restore in .finally of the returned promise, 1–2 microtask settles per flush) — the behavior-spec's 'fake setTimeout' pin, applied to the one global the production code actually calls; each continuation is flushed explicitly so superseded-task-dead / live-task-applies interleavings are individually assertable (WF-I1.2)

B-04 (rev) template pin updated in place rather than deferred: a settled CR disposition (W-10) that moves markup is a supersession of the v1 pin, not a conflict — the updated pin now asserts BOTH the new location AND the absence of the role on .progress, so a regression in either direction fails
CSS comment reworded ('.progress-fill' → 'the old 8px fill rule') because the success-criteria grep is literal and the comment would have kept rg 'progress-fill' non-zero

tempoSuggestion data field lands in Phase 4 (D-H pins all three fields now) though its hint

and consumer are Phase 6 — an unused reactive field for two phases is cheaper than a Phase-6 data-file edit next to the hint wiring
learnings: NEW learning doc 2026-08-24-in-page-poll-loggers-cannot-order-sub-period-events.md — the pinned 5 ms in-page transition logger cannot ORDER two one-shot transitions closer together than the poll period (P(no sample in the gap) ≈ gap/period); the fix is in-page MutationObservers recording each attribute change at its exact performance.now() (deterministic when the transitions land in separate Vue flushes, which the setTimeout(0) yield guarantees). The gap must be computed in tick units (microtask vs macrotask apart) BEFORE choosing the capture mechanism — the plan itself prescribed the wrong tool for E2E-3.1 and the deviation was caught at authoring by arithmetic, not by a red test

Secondary pattern in the same doc: FIFO setTimeout swap (withPinnedYields) for deterministically driving a production-pinned setTimeout(0) yield in unit tests — async functions run synchronously to their first await, so the yield callback is queued by the time the caller resolves; restore in .finally of the returned promise (the run body is async) and settle 1–2 extra microtasks after each flush

Cross-suite template-pin coupling: a markup-contract change (W-10 role move) silently obsoletes a DOMParser template pin in ANOTHER suite (BeatDotsTest B-04 rev) — the plan's file list did not mention it; the 'fully green' baseline criterion is what caught it. When a change moves markup that any Test.html page fetches/pins, grep the test pages for the selector before declaring GREEN (instance of the existing 'grep the test surface for a changed contract' discipline)
Grep success criteria are literal — a CSS comment naming the deleted class (.progress-fill) keeps the grep non-zero; reword comments that reference deliberately-removed identifiers

World-review with nine briefed hypotheses + pre-measured constants (extractPeaks 59 ms, render 0.006 ms) → zero action items, sixth consecutive clean/near-clean review in this project using that pattern
